system_description.narrative_title: A multitiered shock to energy, finance and tech reshapes geopolitics
system_description.narrative_summary: An Iran-centred war is widening into maritime and regional theatres, disrupting oil and LNG flows and privileging energy producers while forcing shipping reroutes and defence coalitions. At the same time a US–China strategic rivalry — especially over AI and chips — collides with a Chinese growth slowdown, amplifying market volatility as bond yields spike, central banks fracture and risk assets reprioritise. These interacting shocks cascade through supply chains (earthquakes, Black Sea attacks, factory weakness), migration pressures in Europe, and corporate strategies, producing a single open system under continuous stress and rapid reconfiguration.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and their militaries; major-power strategic competition (US, China, Russia, Iran, Gulf states); global energy and maritime flows (oil, LNG, chokepoints); international financial markets and central banks (rates, bond markets, FX); global technology/AI and semiconductor supply chains; transnational humanitarian and migration flows; multinational corporations and commodity traders.
system_description.super_system: The global political‑economic system: the international order of states, markets, supply chains, financial institutions and transnational flows on which contemporary geopolitics and globalisation rest.
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy & maritime security (Hormuz, Red Sea, Suez, Black Sea)
Global financial system and central banking (Treasuries, bond markets, FX, Fed/BOJ/ECB dynamics)
US–China technological and industrial competition (AI, chips, trade decoupling)
Regional conflict complexes (Middle East war theatres; Russia–Ukraine war and associated strikes)

variables.name: US–Iran regional war and maritime escalation
variables.description: The United States, Iran and their regional proxies are locked in a widening military confrontation that is shifting control of sea lanes and raising the risk of broader escalation across the Middle East.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and battlefield attrition
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain engaged in high-intensity warfare whose evolving tactics, strikes and external military support are altering frontlines, logistics and the conflict’s trajectory.

variables.name: US–China strategic tech and AI rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting global dominance in semiconductors, artificial intelligence, data and related export controls, reshaping supply chains, standards and market access.

variables.name: Global energy market reconfiguration
variables.description: Producers, national buyers and major oil and gas firms are reorganizing trade flows, refining and LNG capacity and strategic stockpiles in response to sanctions, supply shocks and shifting investment incentives.

variables.name: Monetary policy credibility and bond-market stress
variables.description: Major central banks and financial markets are experiencing rising yields, policy dissent and occasional currency interventions that are reshaping expectations about inflation, rates and central-bank authority.
